answer:
## Headline answer
**Odds ratio of BCG (vs Placebo) on COVID-19/AE severity = 1.64 (95% CI 1.24–2.16, p = 0.0005)** — proportional-odds cumulative-logit model with BCG + prior-MH count + centred patients-interaction frequency + BCG×interaction product term, one row per subject, n = 791, evaluated at the **mean interaction frequency (35.5 patients)** because the interaction term is in the model. Other terms: prior-MH count OR 1.35/condition (1.19–1.52); interaction frequency OR 1.001/patient (0.99–1.01); BCG×frequency OR 0.998/patient (LR p = 0.74 → no interaction). "Severity" here is AE grade (AESEV), not a documented COVID severity scale.

### ⚠️ One implementation finding before you quote any number
My first fits were wrong and my own cross-check caught it: **`statsmodels.miscmodels.ordinal_model.OrderedModel` defaults to `distr='normal'`, i.e. a proportional-PROBIT model**, so `exp(coef)` from a default-args fit is *not* an odds ratio (it returns 1.323, CI 1.12–1.56). All headline numbers use `distr="logit"`; the probit figure is kept only as a labelled implementation-check row so nobody re-derives it. I also re-verified the sign convention (β>0 ⇒ higher severity category) and built an independent cumulative-logit MLE (analytic gradient, self-tested against central differences to 1e-9) that reproduces every statsmodels fit: **max |Δβ| = 9.3e-8** across all subject-level rows.

## 1. Primary model — coefficients / ORs with CIs
`sev ~ bcg + mh_count + ps_c + bcg:ps_c` · PO cumulative logit · n = 791 subjects (209 excluded, no graded AE) · 4 ordered levels · converged = True · logLik = −737.2065 · centring constant 35.487 patients.

| term | β | SE | OR | 95% CI | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **bcg (BCG vs Placebo)** | 0.4918 | 0.1416 | **1.6353** | 1.239 – 2.158 | 0.00051 |
| mh_count (per condition) | 0.2979 | 0.0610 | 1.3471 | 1.195 – 1.518 | <0.0001 |
| ps_c (per patient seen, centred) | 0.0013 | 0.0046 | 1.0013 | 0.992 – 1.010 | 0.785 |
| bcg × ps_c | −0.0020 | 0.0060 | 0.9980 | 0.986 – 1.010 | 0.736 |

Cutpoints 0.232 (1|2), 1.070 (2|3), 0.261 (3|4). Fit quality: observed vs predicted counts by arm agree closely (BCG 160/239/28/10 observed vs 160.3/236.9/28.1/11.8 predicted; Placebo 168/163/15/8 vs 166.1/166.0/15.6/6.3). Predicted at mean covariates: P(sev≥2) 0.525 → 0.643 (RD +11.9 pts), P(sev≥3) 0.056 → 0.089 (RD +3.3 pts); mean worst grade 1.744 (BCG) vs 1.613 (Placebo).

## 2. Interaction: null, stated explicitly
LR χ²(1) = 0.114, **p = 0.736**; Wald χ²(1) = 0.114, p = 0.736; interaction OR 0.9980/patient (0.904 per 50-patient band step). Band-specific simple BCG ORs: 1–50 (n=658) **1.669** (1.23–2.26, p=0.0009); 51–100 (n=108) **1.508** (0.87–2.60, p=0.14); >100 (n=25) **1.363** (0.46–4.07, p=0.58). Monotone but not significant anywhere, CIs heavily overlapping. Dropping the product term leaves the BCG OR identical to four decimals (1.6353) — centring makes the main effect the mean-exposure effect. For the record the *uncentred* refit gives 1.757 "at 0 patients seen", outside the observed range, and is not the reported number.

## 3. Proportional-odds diagnostics (final sample)
Allison/Brant-style heterogeneity Wald over the three cumulative logits: **bcg χ²(3)=0.63 p=0.889 PASS**, ps_c p=0.791 PASS, bcg×ps_c p=0.548 PASS, **mh_count χ²(3)=10.16 p=0.017 FAIL**. mh_count cut-specific ORs rise monotonically — 1.243 (sev>1) → 1.685 (sev>2) → 1.803 (sev>3): comorbidity matters progressively more at the severe end — whereas BCG is flat (1.64 → 1.58 → 1.11 with widening SEs). BCG passes PO so the PO fit stays primary; non-PO estimates as robustness:

| model form | rows | BCG OR (95% CI) | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| PO cumulative logit (primary) | 791 | **1.635 (1.239–2.158)** | 0.0005 |
| stacked cumulative-logit (AMM) | 2373 | 1.602 (1.248–2.056) | 0.0002 |
| continuation-ratio stacked logit | 1315 | 1.514 (1.175–1.951) | 0.0013 |
| partial-PO (cut-specific mh_count) | 2373 | 1.591 (1.242–2.039) | 0.0002 |

BCG sits at 1.51–1.64 across all four: the parallel-lines failure is confined to the adjustment covariate and does not move the answer.

## 4. Sensitivity table
| specification | unit | n | BCG OR (95% CI) | p_bcg | interaction OR (p) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PRIMARY** all graded AEs, max AESEV, MH = all positives | subject | 791 | **1.635 (1.239–2.158)** | 0.0005 | 0.998 (0.74) |
| exclude injection-site reactions | subject | 725 | 1.375 (1.035–1.827) | 0.028 | 0.997 (0.66) |
| RTI-category AEs only | subject | 529 | 1.354 (0.964–1.901) | 0.081 | 1.002 (0.82) |
| COVID-coded AEs only | subject | 153 | 1.225 (0.649–2.311) | 0.532 | 1.006 (0.59) **LOW POWER** |
| **209 ungraded subjects as bottom category 0** | subject | 1000 | **2.372 (1.875–3.001)** | <0.0001 | 1.001 (0.91) |
| MH restricted to chronic comorbidity items | subject | 791 | 1.571 (1.192–2.070) | 0.0013 | 0.999 (0.80) |
| MH = ongoing only (MHONGO=='Yes') | subject | 791 | 1.637 (1.240–2.161) | 0.0005 | 0.998 (0.76) |
| expect_interact (binary) instead of band | subject | 791 | 1.631 (1.235–2.154) | 0.0006 | 1.396 (0.25) |
| unit = one row per AE record | AE | 2063 | 1.177 (0.958–1.447) | 0.122 | 0.995; cluster-robust SEs by USUBJID |
| implementation check: probit link | subject | 791 | 1.323 (1.124–1.557) | 0.0008 | **not an OR — do not quote** |

All rows converged and reproduced the independent MLE to 1e-8 (including the 5-level and AE-level rows — the latter after I fixed a coding bug in my own helper that assumed 1-based category codes). Restricted-MH rule dropped 483/1031 positive rows (383 fixed non-comorbidity items, 42 symptom-only, 30 acute-infection, 24 allergy/atopy, 4 drug/allergen), changing 358 subjects' counts; per-term audit in `mh_term_classification.csv`.

## 5. Plain reading
BCG-vaccinated healthcare workers had **~64% higher odds of a more severe AE-grade category than Placebo** (OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.24–2.16, p=0.0005) at the sample-mean interaction frequency of 35.5 patients; each additional prior medical-history condition raised the odds of a worse grade by 35%, while interaction frequency itself was null and did not modify the BCG effect (product term p=0.74, effect essentially constant across bands at 1.67/1.51/1.36). **Three material caveats:** (i) this is descriptive, not causal, and the **direction contradicts the published BCG-CORONA findings** (BCG protective), so it is a property of this dataset — plausibly synthetic/scrambled — not vaccine-effect evidence; (ii) the headline is **conditional on excluding the 209 subjects with no severity grade** — re-adding them as a bottom "no graded AE" category inflates the OR to 2.37, and because 62% of ungraded rows are injection-site reactions that category blends a grading artefact with severity; (iii) "severity" is AE grade (AESEV 1–4) rather than a documented COVID-19 scale — restricting to COVID-coded AEs leaves 153 subjects and a non-significant 1.22 (0.65–2.31), and the AE-level unit gives 1.18 (0.96–1.45) with cluster-robust SEs, so part of the significance is a unit-of-analysis effect.

Deliverables: `analysis/run_final_model.py` (executed, read-only on `data/`) plus `analysis/results/` (analysis_log.txt and the primary-coefficient, band-specific, PO-diagnostic, model-form robustness, sensitivity, predicted-probability and MH-classification CSVs).

payload.answer: OR = 1.64 (95% CI 1.24-2.16; p = 0.0005) for BCG vs Placebo on ordinal AE severity from a proportional-odds cumulative-logit (ordered logistic) model containing BCG + prior medical-history count + centred patients-interaction frequency + BCG x interaction, n = 791 subjects (one row per subject, worst AESEV), evaluated at the mean interaction frequency (35.5 patients); MH count OR 1.35 per condition, interaction-frequency OR 1.001 per patient, BCG x frequency OR 0.998 per patient (LR p = 0.74, no interaction); proportional odds holds for BCG (p = 0.89), continuation-ratio/partial-PO robustness 1.51-1.64.
